def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-varianc.claim:
Fix a finite horizon $T$. At each $0\le t\le T$, let $\pi_t$ be a probability law on a measurable particle space $\Theta_t$. Let $\widetilde\pi_0$ be an initial proposal with $\pi_0\ll\widetilde\pi_0$, and fix $\upsilon_0=d\pi_0/d\widetilde\pi_0$. For $1\le t\le T$, let $k_t$ be a probability kernel from $\Theta_{t-1}$ to $\Theta_t$, and put
$$\widetilde\pi_t(A)=\int_{\Theta_{t-1}}k_t(x,A)\,\pi_{t-1}(dx).$$
Assume $\pi_t\ll\widetilde\pi_t$ and fix a nonnegative Radon–Nikodym version $\upsilon_t=d\pi_t/d\widetilde\pi_t$, so $\widetilde\pi_t(\upsilon_t)=1$. The BCS-41 sequential importance-resampling algorithm [[alg-sequential-importance-resampling]] is this scheme on path spaces when $k_t$ appends a proposal transition and $\upsilon_t$ is the normalized Feynman–Kac path weight supplied by [[thm-feynman-kac-path-radon-nikodym-weight]].

For a measurable vector function $\phi:\Theta_t\to\mathbb R^d$, write $\mu(\phi)=\int\phi\,d\mu$ and
$$\operatorname{Cov}_{\mu}(\phi)=\int(\phi-\mu(\phi))(\phi-\mu(\phi))^\top\,d\mu,$$
when the second moment is finite. Also write $k_t\phi(x)=\int\phi(z)k_t(x,dz)$ and
$$\operatorname{Cov}_{k_t}(\phi)(x)=\int(\phi(z)-k_t\phi(x))(\phi(z)-k_t\phi(x))^\top k_t(x,dz).$$

The source recursive test classes are
$$\Phi_0^{(d)}=\{\phi:\widetilde\pi_0(\|\phi\|^2)<\infty\},$$
and, for $t\ge1$,
$$\Phi_t^{(d)}=\left\{\phi:\text{ for some }\delta>0,\ \widetilde\pi_t(\|\upsilon_t\phi\|^{2+\delta})<\infty\ \text{ and }\ x\mapsto k_t(\upsilon_t\phi)(x)\in\Phi_{t-1}^{(d)}\right\}.$$
Assume $1\in\Phi_t^{(1)}$ for every $t$. This is the source theorem's explicit normalizing-weight condition. For the recursive post-resampling CLTs proved on this page, use the stronger classes $\Psi_t^{(d)}$. At $t=0$, let $\Psi_0^{(d)}$ consist of the $\phi\in\Phi_0^{(d)}$ for which, for some $\epsilon>0$, $\widetilde\pi_0(\|\upsilon_0(\phi-\pi_0(\phi))\|^{2+\epsilon})<\infty$ and $\pi_0(\|\phi\|^{2+\epsilon})<\infty$. The initial normalizing denominator needs only its finite first moment $\widetilde\pi_0(\upsilon_0)=1$. For $t\ge1$, let $\Psi_t^{(d)}$ consist of the $\phi\in\Phi_t^{(d)}$ for which, for some $\epsilon>0$, $\pi_t(\|\phi\|^{2+\epsilon})<\infty$ and $x\mapsto E_t(\phi-\pi_t(\phi))(x)\in\Psi_{t-1}^{(d)}$. Here $E_t h=k_t(\upsilon_t h)$ is the operator defined below. The recursive target moments supply the offspring variance at every earlier selection used in the induction. The source $\Phi_t$ conditions alone need not imply them. The source condition $1\in\Phi_t$ and these recursive target moments are the stated hypotheses for the CLT induction; no higher initial normalizer moment is required.

Define the mutation covariance operators recursively. At time zero,
$$\widetilde V_0(\phi)=\operatorname{Cov}_{\widetilde\pi_0}(\phi).$$
For $t\ge1$,
$$\widetilde V_t(\phi)=\widehat V_{t-1}(k_t\phi)+\int\operatorname{Cov}_{k_t}(\phi)(x)\,\pi_{t-1}(dx).$$
The weighted-estimator covariance is
$$V_t(\phi)=\widetilde V_t\!\left(\upsilon_t(\phi-\pi_t(\phi))\right).$$
For a measurable vector function $h$ on $\Theta_t$, define the forward operator from $\Theta_{t-1}$ by
$$E_t h(x)=k_t(\upsilon_t h)(x)=\int\upsilon_t(z)h(z)\,k_t(x,dz).$$
For $k<t$, write $E_{k+1:t}=E_{k+1}\circ\cdots\circ E_t$; set $E_{t+1:t}$ to the identity operator.
For multinomial offspring resampling set
$$\widehat V_t^{\mathrm{multi}}(\phi)=V_t(\phi)+\operatorname{Cov}_{\pi_t}(\phi).$$
For residual offspring resampling, let $r(u)=u-\lfloor u\rfloor$. When $c_t=\widetilde\pi_t(r(\upsilon_t))>0$, define the formal source candidate
$$R_t^{\mathrm{cand}}(\phi)=\widetilde\pi_t\!\left(r(\upsilon_t)\phi\phi^\top\right)-\frac{\widetilde\pi_t(r(\upsilon_t)\phi)\,\widetilde\pi_t(r(\upsilon_t)\phi)^\top}{c_t}.$$
Set $R_t=R_t^{\mathrm{cand}}$ and $\widehat V_t^{\mathrm{res}}=V_t+R_t$ only when $\widetilde\pi_t(\upsilon_t\in\{1,2,\ldots\})=0$; then $c_t>0$ and the finite-sample floor discontinuities are avoided. If $\upsilon_t=1$ $\widetilde\pi_t$-almost everywhere, all normalized weights are exactly equal and residual offspring are deterministic; in that special case put $R_t=0$. No residual covariance is assigned when $c_t=0$ but $\upsilon_t$ is not almost everywhere one: the finite-sample normalization can move positive integer weights across floor boundaries. The B-page counterexamples show why the general positive-integer-atom branch remains unassigned.

derivations.claim: At time $0$, [F2] and the finite particle law [F7] give IID proposal particles with law $\widetilde\pi_0$. For $h\in L^1(\widetilde\pi_0)$, [F4] gives $\eta_0^N(h)\to\widetilde\pi_0(h)$. If $\phi\in L^1(\pi_0)$, then $\upsilon_0\phi$ is integrable under $\widetilde\pi_0$ and its integral is $\pi_0(\phi)$ by [F1]; also $\widetilde\pi_0(\upsilon_0)=1$. Applying [F4] to numerator and denominator and dividing on the event that the denominator is positive gives $\omega_0^N(\phi)\to\pi_0(\phi)$. That event has probability tending to one because the denominator average converges to $1$.

Fix $t\ge1$ and suppose the three convergences hold at $t-1$. First let $h$ be bounded. By [F2] and [F7], conditional on the selected parents, the $X_t^i$ are independent with laws $k_t(\check X_{t-1}^i,\cdot)$; measurability of $k_th$ follows from [F8]. Thus $\eta_t^N(h)-\check\eta_{t-1}^N(k_th)$ has conditional mean zero and conditional variance at most $\|h\|_\infty^2/N$. By [F5] this difference tends to zero in probability. Since $k_th$ is bounded and $\pi_{t-1}(k_th)=\widetilde\pi_t(h)$ by [F1], the induction hypothesis proves $\eta_t^N(h)\to\widetilde\pi_t(h)$.

For general $h\in L^1(\widetilde\pi_t)$, let $h_M=h\mathbf1_{\{|h|\le M\}}$. The conditional mean of $\eta_t^N(|h-h_M|)$ is $Y_N=\check\eta_{t-1}^N(k_t|h-h_M|)$, measurable by [F8]. The function inside this last empirical average is integrable under $\pi_{t-1}$ and its integral is $a_M=\widetilde\pi_t(|h-h_M|)$. The induction hypothesis gives $Y_N\to a_M$ in probability. Conditional Markov [F6] bounds $P(\eta_t^N(|h-h_M|)>\epsilon)$ by $E[\min(1,Y_N/\epsilon)]$. For fixed $M$, bounded continuity of $y\mapsto\min(1,y/\epsilon)$ and convergence in probability to the constant $a_M$ imply that this expectation tends to $\min(1,a_M/\epsilon)$: for any $\eta>0$, split on $|Y_N-a_M|\le\eta$ and its complement, use continuity on the first event and convergence in probability on the second. Since $a_M\to0$ by integrability, the limiting tail probability vanishes. Applying the same truncation to the target integral and combining with step 2.1 proves the proposal empirical convergence for every integrable $h$.

Apply step 2.2 to $h=\upsilon_t$ and $h=\upsilon_t\phi$, where $\phi\in L^1(\pi_t)$. Their limiting integrals are $1$ and $\pi_t(\phi)$ by [F1]. The ratio consequently converges to $\pi_t(\phi)$ whenever its denominator is positive; the denominator-zero event has probability tending to zero because its normalized sum converges to $1$. The uniform fallback in [F2] on that event cannot change convergence in probability.

For bounded $\phi$, the conditional expectation of $\check\eta_t^N(\phi)$ is $\omega_t^N(\phi)$ by [F3]. In multinomial resampling the conditional variance is at most $\|\phi\|_\infty^2/N$. In residual resampling the deterministic floor counts contribute no variance, and the remaining $R\le N$ categorical draws give conditional variance at most $\|\phi\|_\infty^2/N$ as well. Chebyshev [F5] and step 3.1 prove $\check\eta_t^N(\phi)\to\pi_t(\phi)$ for bounded $\phi$.

For $\phi\in L^1(\pi_t)$, truncate to $\phi_M=\phi\mathbf1_{\{|\phi|\le M\}}$. By [F3], the conditional expected selected average of $|\phi-\phi_M|$ is exactly $\omega_t^N(|\phi-\phi_M|)$. Combining with step 4.1 proves the selected empirical convergence for all integrable $\phi$.

derivations.claim: Let $\mathcal F_N$ contain the corrected particles and their weights. By [F2], conditionally on $\mathcal F_N$ the selected values $Y_1^N,\ldots,Y_N^N$ are IID with law $\omega_t^N$. Their centered conditional variance is $s_N^2=\omega_t^N(\phi^2)-\omega_t^N(\phi)^2$, which converges in probability to $s^2=\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_t}(\phi)$ by [F1] and [F3].

Put $\xi_i^N=\phi(Y_i^N)-\omega_t^N(\phi)$. Since $\pi_t(|\phi|^{2+\epsilon})<\infty$, [F3] gives $\omega_t^N(|\phi|^{2+\epsilon})=O_P(1)$ and $\omega_t^N(|\phi|)=O_P(1)$. Jensen's inequality and $|a-b|^{2+\epsilon}\le 2^{1+\epsilon}(|a|^{2+\epsilon}+|b|^{2+\epsilon})$ then give $\omega_t^N(|\phi-\omega_t^N(\phi)|^{2+\epsilon})=O_P(1)$. For every $a>0$, the conditional Lindeberg sum is bounded by
$$\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\mathbb E\!\left[(\xi_i^N)^2\mathbf1_{\{|\xi_i^N|>a\sqrt N\}}\middle|\mathcal F_N\right]\le a^{-\epsilon}N^{-\epsilon/2}\omega_t^N(|\phi-\omega_t^N(\phi)|^{2+\epsilon}),$$

If $s>0$, then eventually $s_N>s/2$; the normalized Lindeberg sum for draws divided by $s_N\sqrt N$ is bounded by step 1.2 at threshold $as/2$, divided by $s_N^2$. It therefore tends to zero in probability, and a further subsequence makes that convergence almost sure. Apply [F4] to obtain a standard-normal limit for the normalized row. If its variance is positive, [F4] gives the IID CLT; if its variance is zero, [F6] gives convergence of its centered sample mean to zero. The same arguments together with the target-moment condition show closure of $\Psi_t$. If $\phi\in\Psi_t$, then $\psi=\upsilon_t(\phi-\pi_t\phi)$ has a finite proposal $2+\delta$ moment because $\phi,1\in\Phi_t$, and $k_t\psi=E_t(\phi-\pi_t\phi)\in\Psi_{t-1}$ by the recursive $\Psi_t$ condition.

For the mutation part, condition on the selected parent paths $\check X_{t-1}^{1:N}$ and set $m_i=k_t\psi(\check X_{t-1}^i)$. Under the product kernel in [F2], $D_{i,N}=\psi(X_t^i)-m_i$ are independent and centered. Their row variance is
$$s_N^2=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\operatorname{Var}_{k_t(\check X_{t-1}^i)}(\psi),$$
which converges in probability to $\sigma^2=\pi_{t-1}(\operatorname{Var}_{k_t}(\psi))$ by [F3], because $0\le\operatorname{Var}_{k_t}(\psi)\le k_t(\psi^2)$ and $\pi_{t-1}(k_t|\psi|^{2+\delta})=\widetilde\pi_t(|\psi|^{2+\delta})<\infty$. $$C_\delta a^{-\delta}N^{-\delta/2}s_N^{-(2+\delta)}\,\check\eta_{t-1}^N(k_t|\psi|^{2+\delta}),$$
where $C_\delta$ is a finite constant from $|a-b|^{2+\delta}\le2^{1+\delta}(|a|^{2+\delta}+|b|^{2+\delta})$ and Jensen's inequality. Since $s_N\to\sigma>0$ and [F3] makes the average factor converge in probability to a finite value, this conditional Lindeberg sum tends to zero.

Define the mutation covariance operators recursively. At time zero,
$$\widetilde V_0(\phi)=\operatorname{Cov}_{\widetilde\pi_0}(\phi).$$
For $t\ge1$,
$$\widetilde V_t(\phi)=\widehat V_{t-1}(k_t\phi)+\int\operatorname{Cov}_{k_t}(\phi)(x)\,\pi_{t-1}(dx).$$
The weighted-estimator covariance is
$$V_t(\phi)=\widetilde V_t\!\left(\upsilon_t(\phi-\pi_t(\phi))\right).$$
For a measurable vector function $h$ on $\Theta_t$, define the forward operator from $\Theta_{t-1}$ by
$$E_t h(x)=k_t(\upsilon_t h)(x)=\int\upsilon_t(z)h(z)\,k_t(x,dz).$$
For $k<t$, write $E_{k+1:t}=E_{k+1}\circ\cdots\circ E_t$; set $E_{t+1:t}$ to the identity operator.
For multinomial offspring resampling set
$$\widehat V_t^{\mathrm{multi}}(\phi)=V_t(\phi)+\operatorname{Cov}_{\pi_t}(\phi).$$
For residual offspring resampling, let $r(u)=u-\lfloor u\rfloor$. When $c_t=\widetilde\pi_t(r(\upsilon_t))>0$, define the formal source candidate
$$R_t^{\mathrm{cand}}(\phi)=\widetilde\pi_t\!\left(r(\upsilon_t)\phi\phi^\top\right)-\frac{\widetilde\pi_t(r(\upsilon_t)\phi)\,\widetilde\pi_t(r(\upsilon_t)\phi)^\top}{c_t}.$$
Set $R_t=R_t^{\mathrm{cand}}$ and $\widehat V_t^{\mathrm{res}}=V_t+R_t$ only when $\widetilde\pi_t(\upsilon_t\in\{1,2,\ldots\})=0$; then $c_t>0$ and the finite-sample floor discontinuities are avoided. If $\upsilon_t=1$ $\widetilde\pi_t$-almost everywhere, all normalized weights are exactly equal and residual offspring are deterministic; in that special case put $R_t=0$. No residual covariance is assigned when $c_t=0$ but $\upsilon_t$ is not almost everywhere one: the finite-sample normalization can move positive integer weights across floor boundaries. The B-page counterexamples show why the general positive-integer-atom branch remains unassigned.

For multinomial resampling, return the sampled vector $(J_1,\ldots,J_N)$ in its sampled order, together with its count vector $(C_1,\ldots,C_N)$; do not sort the sampled indices. For residual resampling, return the ancestor list containing exactly $C_j$ copies of index $j$, ordered by increasing index, together with its count vector. Each output is a length-$N$ list and a count vector summing to $N$. When all input weights vanish, the uniform fallback defines the procedure; any downstream normalizer already multiplied by this zero average remains zero.
Assume AC. Let $(X_k)_{k\ge1}$ be iid real random variables with mean $m$ and variance $0<\sigma^2<\infty$. Then $$\frac{\sum_{k=1}^nX_k-nm}{\sigma\sqrt n}\ \Rightarrow\ N(0,1).$$

Let $(X_n)$ and $(Y_n)$ be real random variables on one probability space, and let $X$ be a real random variable (possibly on another space). If $X_n\Rightarrow X$ and $Y_n\to c$ in probability for $c\in\mathbb R$, then $X_n+Y_n\Rightarrow X+c$ and $X_nY_n\Rightarrow cX$. If $c\ne0$, define $Q_n=X_n/Y_n$ on $\{Y_n\ne0\}$ and give $Q_n$ any fixed value on $\{Y_n=0\}$. Then $Q_n\Rightarrow X/c$.

Let S,T be metric spaces, $g:S\to T$ measurable, and $\mu_n\Rightarrow\mu$. If the discontinuity set $D_g$ is $\mu$-null, then $g_*\mu_n\Rightarrow g_*\mu$. Consequently $X_n\Rightarrow X$ implies $g(X_n)\Rightarrow g(X)$ whenever $P_X(D_g)=0$.

derivations.claim:
For $N$ IID proposal particles, let $M_N$ be the number at $A$ and $p_N=M_N/N$. The weighted empirical estimate is
$$S_N=\frac{2M_N}{2M_N+(2/3)(N-M_N)}=\frac{3p_N}{1+2p_N}.$$
Since $M_N$ is binomial with parameters $(N,1/4)$, [F3] gives $\sqrt N(p_N-1/4)\Rightarrow N(0,3/16)$. The identity $\sqrt N(S_N-1/2)=2\sqrt N(p_N-1/4)/(1+2p_N)$ and [F4] yield $Z_N:=\sqrt N(S_N-1/2)\Rightarrow Z\sim N(0,1/3)$. Moreover, $Z_N>0$ exactly when $p_N>1/4$.

The limiting-weight candidate in [F1] gives $r(2)=0$ and $r(2/3)=2/3$. Because $\phi(B)=0$, both $\widetilde\pi_0(r(\upsilon_0)\phi^2)$ and $\widetilde\pi_0(r(\upsilon_0)\phi)$ are zero, so $R_0^{\mathrm{cand}}(\phi)=0$. If used as a universal residual CLT variance, it predicts a post-resampling Gaussian limit with variance $V_0(\phi)=\widetilde\pi_0[\upsilon_0^2(\phi-1/2)^2]=1/3$.

Put $\bar w_N=2/3+(4/3)p_N$ and $u_A=2/\bar w_N$, $u_B=(2/3)/\bar w_N$. On $1/4<p_N<1/3$, the normalized residual sizes are $u_A\in(1,2)$ and $u_B\in(0,1)$; hence each $A$ particle receives one deterministic child, each $B$ particle receives none, and $R=N-M_N$ children are sampled from the remainders. If $X_N$ is the number of residual children at $A$, then conditionally on the proposal sample, $X_N\sim\mathrm{Bin}(R,a_N)$ with $a_N=M_N(u_A-1)/R$. As $p_N\downarrow1/4$, $R/N\to3/4$ and $a_N\to1/3$.

On that event, the post-resampling mean is $(M_N+X_N)/N$ and its conditional mean is $S_N$. A Taylor expansion of the binomial characteristic function, uniform for $0\le a_N\le1$ and $R\le N$, gives
$$\mathbb E\!\left[\exp\!\left(iu\frac{X_N-Ra_N}{\sqrt N}\right)\middle|M_N\right]=\exp\!\left(-\frac{u^2}{2}\frac RN a_N(1-a_N)+O(N^{-1/2})\right).$$
Thus, on the positive branch $p_N>1/4$, the extra resampling fluctuation has limiting variance $(3/4)(1/3)(2/3)=1/6$.

On the negative branch with $p_N<1/4$ and $p_N\to1/4$, one has $u_A\in(2,3)$ and $u_B\in(0,1)$. The floor for each $A$ particle is two, and its total fractional remainder is $M_N(u_A-2)=O_P(\sqrt N)$, because $u_A-2=2(1/\bar w_N-1)=O_P(|p_N-1/4|)$. Conditional variance of the residual $A$ count is at most this total remainder. Consequently the variance of $\sqrt N$ times the post-resampling proportion about its weighted conditional mean is $O_P(N^{-1/2})$, so the extra resampling fluctuation tends to zero in probability on the negative branch. The events $p_N\notin(1/5,1/3)$ have probability tending to zero by [F3].

Put $U_N=\sqrt N(\check\eta_0^N(\phi)-S_N)$, the post-resampling fluctuation centered at the weighted mean, and condition on the proposal count $M_N$. For any real $v,s$, steps 2.2–3.1 and the negligible exceptional event show that $\mathbb E[e^{isU_N}\mid M_N]$ converges in probability to $e^{-s^2/12}$ when $Z_N>0$ and to $1$ when $Z_N<0$. Since $Z_N\Rightarrow Z$ and $P(Z=0)=0$, [F5] gives
$$\mathbb E[e^{ivZ_N+isU_N}]\longrightarrow\mathbb E\!\left[e^{ivZ}\left(\mathbf1_{\{Z>0\}}e^{-s^2/12}+\mathbf1_{\{Z<0\}}\right)\right].$$
This is the joint characteristic function of $(Z,\mathbf1_{\{Z>0\}}W)$ for an independent $W\sim N(0,1/6)$, so the post-resampling limit is $Z+\mathbf1_{\{Z>0\}}W$. Its mean is zero and its third moment is $3\mathbb E[Z\mathbf1_{\{Z>0\}}]\mathbb E[W^2]>0$, so it is not Gaussian. This contradicts the variance-$1/3$ Gaussian predicted in step 1.2.

finite_checks.claim:
For $N$ IID proposal particles, let $M_N$ be the number at $A$ and $p_N=M_N/N$. The weighted empirical estimate is
$$S_N=\frac{2M_N}{2M_N+(2/3)(N-M_N)}=\frac{3p_N}{1+2p_N}.$$
Since $M_N$ is binomial with parameters $(N,1/4)$, [F3] gives $\sqrt N(p_N-1/4)\Rightarrow N(0,3/16)$. The identity $\sqrt N(S_N-1/2)=2\sqrt N(p_N-1/4)/(1+2p_N)$ and [F4] yield $Z_N:=\sqrt N(S_N-1/2)\Rightarrow Z\sim N(0,1/3)$. Moreover, $Z_N>0$ exactly when $p_N>1/4$.
finite_checks.result: Computed and justified in proof step 1.1.

finite_checks.claim: The limiting-weight candidate in [F1] gives $r(2)=0$ and $r(2/3)=2/3$. Because $\phi(B)=0$, both $\widetilde\pi_0(r(\upsilon_0)\phi^2)$ and $\widetilde\pi_0(r(\upsilon_0)\phi)$ are zero, so $R_0^{\mathrm{cand}}(\phi)=0$. If used as a universal residual CLT variance, it predicts a post-resampling Gaussian limit with variance $V_0(\phi)=\widetilde\pi_0[\upsilon_0^2(\phi-1/2)^2]=1/3$.
finite_checks.result: Computed and justified in proof step 1.2.

finite_checks.claim: Put $\bar w_N=2/3+(4/3)p_N$ and $u_A=2/\bar w_N$, $u_B=(2/3)/\bar w_N$. On $1/4<p_N<1/3$, the normalized residual sizes are $u_A\in(1,2)$ and $u_B\in(0,1)$; hence each $A$ particle receives one deterministic child, each $B$ particle receives none, and $R=N-M_N$ children are sampled from the remainders. If $X_N$ is the number of residual children at $A$, then conditionally on the proposal sample, $X_N\sim\mathrm{Bin}(R,a_N)$ with $a_N=M_N(u_A-1)/R$. As $p_N\downarrow1/4$, $R/N\to3/4$ and $a_N\to1/3$.
finite_checks.result: Computed and justified in proof step 2.1.

finite_checks.claim:
On that event, the post-resampling mean is $(M_N+X_N)/N$ and its conditional mean is $S_N$. A Taylor expansion of the binomial characteristic function, uniform for $0\le a_N\le1$ and $R\le N$, gives
$$\mathbb E\!\left[\exp\!\left(iu\frac{X_N-Ra_N}{\sqrt N}\right)\middle|M_N\right]=\exp\!\left(-\frac{u^2}{2}\frac RN a_N(1-a_N)+O(N^{-1/2})\right).$$
Thus, on the positive branch $p_N>1/4$, the extra resampling fluctuation has limiting variance $(3/4)(1/3)(2/3)=1/6$.
finite_checks.result: Computed and justified in proof step 2.2.

finite_checks.claim: On the negative branch with $p_N<1/4$ and $p_N\to1/4$, one has $u_A\in(2,3)$ and $u_B\in(0,1)$. The floor for each $A$ particle is two, and its total fractional remainder is $M_N(u_A-2)=O_P(\sqrt N)$, because $u_A-2=2(1/\bar w_N-1)=O_P(|p_N-1/4|)$. Conditional variance of the residual $A$ count is at most this total remainder. Consequently the variance of $\sqrt N$ times the post-resampling proportion about its weighted conditional mean is $O_P(N^{-1/2})$, so the extra resampling fluctuation tends to zero in probability on the negative branch. The events $p_N\notin(1/5,1/3)$ have probability tending to zero by [F3].

finite_checks.claim:
Put $U_N=\sqrt N(\check\eta_0^N(\phi)-S_N)$, the post-resampling fluctuation centered at the weighted mean, and condition on the proposal count $M_N$. For any real $v,s$, steps 2.2–3.1 and the negligible exceptional event show that $\mathbb E[e^{isU_N}\mid M_N]$ converges in probability to $e^{-s^2/12}$ when $Z_N>0$ and to $1$ when $Z_N<0$. Since $Z_N\Rightarrow Z$ and $P(Z=0)=0$, [F5] gives
$$\mathbb E[e^{ivZ_N+isU_N}]\longrightarrow\mathbb E\!\left[e^{ivZ}\left(\mathbf1_{\{Z>0\}}e^{-s^2/12}+\mathbf1_{\{Z<0\}}\right)\right].$$
This is the joint characteristic function of $(Z,\mathbf1_{\{Z>0\}}W)$ for an independent $W\sim N(0,1/6)$, so the post-resampling limit is $Z+\mathbf1_{\{Z>0\}}W$. Its mean is zero and its third moment is $3\mathbb E[Z\mathbf1_{\{Z>0\}}]\mathbb E[W^2]>0$, so it is not Gaussian. This contradicts the variance-$1/3$ Gaussian predicted in step 1.2.
finite_checks.result: Computed and justified in proof step 3.2.

Fix a finite horizon $T$. At each $0\le t\le T$, let $\pi_t$ be a probability law on a measurable particle space $\Theta_t$. Let $\widetilde\pi_0$ be an initial proposal with $\pi_0\ll\widetilde\pi_0$, and fix $\upsilon_0=d\pi_0/d\widetilde\pi_0$. For $1\le t\le T$, let $k_t$ be a probability kernel from $\Theta_{t-1}$ to $\Theta_t$, and put
$$\widetilde\pi_t(A)=\int_{\Theta_{t-1}}k_t(x,A)\,\pi_{t-1}(dx).$$
Assume $\pi_t\ll\widetilde\pi_t$ and fix a nonnegative Radon–Nikodym version $\upsilon_t=d\pi_t/d\widetilde\pi_t$, so $\widetilde\pi_t(\upsilon_t)=1$. The BCS-41 sequential importance-resampling algorithm [[alg-sequential-importance-resampling]] is this scheme on path spaces when $k_t$ appends a proposal transition and $\upsilon_t$ is the normalized Feynman–Kac path weight supplied by [[thm-feynman-kac-path-radon-nikodym-weight]].

For multinomial resampling, return the sampled vector $(J_1,\ldots,J_N)$ in its sampled order, together with its count vector $(C_1,\ldots,C_N)$; do not sort the sampled indices. For residual resampling, return the ancestor list containing exactly $C_j$ copies of index $j$, ordered by increasing index, together with its count vector. Each output is a length-$N$ list and a count vector summing to $N$. When all input weights vanish, the uniform fallback defines the procedure; any downstream normalizer already multiplied by this zero average remains zero.

Define the mutation covariance operators recursively. At time zero,
$$\widetilde V_0(\phi)=\operatorname{Cov}_{\widetilde\pi_0}(\phi).$$
For $t\ge1$,
$$\widetilde V_t(\phi)=\widehat V_{t-1}(k_t\phi)+\int\operatorname{Cov}_{k_t}(\phi)(x)\,\pi_{t-1}(dx).$$
The weighted-estimator covariance is
$$V_t(\phi)=\widetilde V_t\!\left(\upsilon_t(\phi-\pi_t(\phi))\right).$$
For a measurable vector function $h$ on $\Theta_t$, define the forward operator from $\Theta_{t-1}$ by
$$E_t h(x)=k_t(\upsilon_t h)(x)=\int\upsilon_t(z)h(z)\,k_t(x,dz).$$
For $k<t$, write $E_{k+1:t}=E_{k+1}\circ\cdots\circ E_t$; set $E_{t+1:t}$ to the identity operator.
For multinomial offspring resampling set
$$\widehat V_t^{\mathrm{multi}}(\phi)=V_t(\phi)+\operatorname{Cov}_{\pi_t}(\phi).$$
For residual offspring resampling, let $r(u)=u-\lfloor u\rfloor$. When $c_t=\widetilde\pi_t(r(\upsilon_t))>0$, define the formal source candidate
$$R_t^{\mathrm{cand}}(\phi)=\widetilde\pi_t\!\left(r(\upsilon_t)\phi\phi^\top\right)-\frac{\widetilde\pi_t(r(\upsilon_t)\phi)\,\widetilde\pi_t(r(\upsilon_t)\phi)^\top}{c_t}.$$
Set $R_t=R_t^{\mathrm{cand}}$ and $\widehat V_t^{\mathrm{res}}=V_t+R_t$ only when $\widetilde\pi_t(\upsilon_t\in\{1,2,\ldots\})=0$; then $c_t>0$ and the finite-sample floor discontinuities are avoided. If $\upsilon_t=1$ $\widetilde\pi_t$-almost everywhere, all normalized weights are exactly equal and residual offspring are deterministic; in that special case put $R_t=0$. No residual covariance is assigned when $c_t=0$ but $\upsilon_t$ is not almost everywhere one: the finite-sample normalization can move positive integer weights across floor boundaries. The B-page counterexamples show why the general positive-integer-atom branch remains unassigned.

Use the operators and multinomial variance recursion of [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]] at every selection time. For $\phi\in\Psi_t^{(d)}$, put $\bar\phi=\phi-\pi_t(\phi)$. Then
$$V_t(\phi)=\sum_{k=0}^{t}\widetilde\pi_k\!\left[\upsilon_k^2\,E_{k+1:t}(\bar\phi)E_{k+1:t}(\bar\phi)^\top\right],$$
where the $k=t$ term uses $E_{t+1:t}\bar\phi=\bar\phi$. Each summand is a finite positive-semidefinite matrix under the stated class conditions.

derivations.claim: For every pair of preceding states, both $g(x\mid x')/g(x\mid x'')$ and $q_t(x\mid x')/q_t(x\mid x'')$ equal $1$. The likelihood satisfies $0<1\le f(\ast\mid x)\le1$, and $\Delta\phi=1$. The filtering target at every $t\ge1$ has last-state law $\pi_t(X_t=1)=1/2$, while the proposal last-state law is $q_t$. Its normalized incremental Radon–Nikodym weight is $\upsilon_t(1)=1/(2\epsilon_t)$ and $\upsilon_t(0)=1/(2(1-\epsilon_t))$.

For every preceding path, the forward image of the centered test is
$$E_t(\phi-1/2)=\sum_{x=0}^1q_t(x\mid x_{t-1})\upsilon_t(x)(\mathbf1_{\{x=1\}}-1/2)=\sum_{x=0}^1g(x\mid x_{t-1})(\mathbf1_{\{x=1\}}-1/2)=0.$$
Consequently $E_{k+1:t}(\phi-\pi_t\phi)=0$ for every $k<t$, so all earlier-time terms in [F2] vanish.

The remaining $k=t$ term in [F2] is
$$V_t(\phi)=\epsilon_t\left(\frac1{2\epsilon_t}\right)^2\frac14+(1-\epsilon_t)\left(\frac1{2(1-\epsilon_t)}\right)^2\frac14=\frac1{16\epsilon_t}+\frac1{16(1-\epsilon_t)}.$$
Since $\epsilon_t=2^{-t-2}\downarrow0$, $V_t(\phi)\to\infty$ despite all the stated ratio, likelihood, and oscillation bounds. Thus those conditions alone do not imply the claimed time-uniform variance bound.

The source recursive test classes are
$$\Phi_0^{(d)}=\{\phi:\widetilde\pi_0(\|\phi\|^2)<\infty\},$$
and, for $t\ge1$,
$$\Phi_t^{(d)}=\left\{\phi:\text{ for some }\delta>0,\ \widetilde\pi_t(\|\upsilon_t\phi\|^{2+\delta})<\infty\ \text{ and }\ x\mapsto k_t(\upsilon_t\phi)(x)\in\Phi_{t-1}^{(d)}\right\}.$$
Assume $1\in\Phi_t^{(1)}$ for every $t$. This is the source theorem's explicit normalizing-weight condition. For the recursive post-resampling CLTs proved on this page, use the stronger classes $\Psi_t^{(d)}$. At $t=0$, let $\Psi_0^{(d)}$ consist of the $\phi\in\Phi_0^{(d)}$ for which, for some $\epsilon>0$, $\widetilde\pi_0(\|\upsilon_0(\phi-\pi_0(\phi))\|^{2+\epsilon})<\infty$ and $\pi_0(\|\phi\|^{2+\epsilon})<\infty$. The initial normalizing denominator needs only its finite first moment $\widetilde\pi_0(\upsilon_0)=1$. For $t\ge1$, let $\Psi_t^{(d)}$ consist of the $\phi\in\Phi_t^{(d)}$ for which, for some $\epsilon>0$, $\pi_t(\|\phi\|^{2+\epsilon})<\infty$ and $x\mapsto E_t(\phi-\pi_t(\phi))(x)\in\Psi_{t-1}^{(d)}$. Here $E_t h=k_t(\upsilon_t h)$ is the operator defined below. The recursive target moments supply the offspring variance at every earlier selection used in the induction. The source $\Phi_t$ conditions alone need not imply them. The source condition $1\in\Phi_t$ and these recursive target moments are the stated hypotheses for the CLT induction; no higher initial normalizer moment is required.

Let $(S,\Sigma)$ and $(E,\mathcal E)$ be measurable spaces with $S\ne\varnothing$, and let $K:S\rightsquigarrow E$ be a probability kernel as in [[def-measure-kernel-and-probability-kernel]]. Its **Dobrushin contraction coefficient** is
$$\delta(K):=\sup_{x,x'\in S}\lVert K(x,\cdot)-K(x',\cdot)\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}},$$
where $\lVert\cdot\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}$ is the event-supremum distance between probability laws in [[def-total-variation-distance-for-probability-laws]]. Thus $0\le\delta(K)\le1$. The coefficient measures the largest total-variation separation between two one-step output laws.

Let $K:S\rightsquigarrow E$ be a probability kernel on a nonempty measurable source space. Suppose a sigma-finite measure $\lambda$ on $E$ and probability densities $k_x$ satisfy $K(x,A)=\int_A k_x\,d\lambda$ for every $x\in S$ and measurable $A\subseteq E$. If $C\ge1$ and, for every $x,x'\in S$, $k_x(z)\le Ck_{x'}(z)$ for $\lambda$-almost every $z$, then the Dobrushin coefficient from [[def-dobrushin-coefficient-for-probability-kernels]] obeys
$$\delta(K)\le1-C^{-1}.$$

Let $E_s$ be the forward operators of [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]], and for bounded real $h$ put $\operatorname{osc}(h)=\sup h-\inf h$. Suppose there is one $\beta\in[0,1)$ such that
$$\operatorname{osc}(E_s h)\le\beta\operatorname{osc}(h)$$
for every $s$ and every bounded real $h$. For bounded $\phi:\Theta_t\to\mathbb R$, put $\Delta\phi=\operatorname{osc}(\phi)$ and $\bar\phi=\phi-\pi_t(\phi)$. Then for every $0\le k\le t$,
$$\bigl\lVert E_{k+1:t}\bar\phi\bigr\rVert_\infty\le\beta^{t-k}\Delta\phi,$$
with $\beta^0=1$ and $E_{t+1:t}$ the identity. This condition concerns the actual SMC backward operators; it is not implied merely by mixing ratios of the proposal densities.

Use multinomial offspring resampling at every time and the variance $V_t$ in [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]]. Assume there is a constant $B<\infty$ such that $\upsilon_s\le B$ $\widetilde\pi_s$-almost everywhere for every $s\ge0$. Assume also that the forward operators satisfy the uniform oscillation condition of [[lem-smc-backward-operator-oscillation-bound]] with one $\beta\in[0,1)$ for all times. Then every bounded real test $\phi$ with $\Delta\phi=\sup\phi-\inf\phi<\infty$ satisfies
$$V_t(\phi)\le\frac{B^2(\Delta\phi)^2}{1-\beta^2}\qquad(t\ge0).$$
This is a bound on the fixed-horizon CLT variance, uniform in the time index; it is not a finite-particle error bound.

derivations.claim: Every transition row is $(1/2,1/2)$, so the target and proposal transitions coincide and the likelihood contributes no correction. By [F1], $\upsilon_s=1$, hence $B=1$, and $\pi_s$ is uniform for every $s\ge0$. Since the row does not depend on its predecessor, [F2] gives $\delta(K)=0$; its density rows are identical, so [F3] also applies with $C=1$.

The forward operator is $E_sh=Kh$, which maps every function to its uniform average. Thus $\operatorname{osc}(E_sh)=0$, so the contraction hypothesis holds with $\beta=0$. The test has $\Delta\phi=1$ and is centered by $1/2$. Every earlier backward image is zero; the final $k=t$ term in the variance expansion is $\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_t}(\phi)=1/4$. Hence $V_t(\phi)=1/4$ for every $t$.

Applying [F5] with $B=1$, $\beta=0$ and $\Delta\phi=1$ gives $V_t(\phi)\le1$, uniformly in $t$; the exact variance $1/4$ from step 1.2 satisfies the bound. This verifies a time-uniform asymptotic-variance result under explicit mixing and weight conditions.

ex-smc-fixed-horizon-clt-does-not-give-t.claim: Let $\mathsf X=\{0,1\}$ have the uniform target and proposal at time zero. Use identity mutation, unit incremental weights, and multinomial resampling at every time. For each fixed horizon $t$, take $\phi(x_{0:t})=\mathbf1_{\{x_t=1\}}$. Compute the fixed-horizon asymptotic variance and compare its dependence on $t$ with a time-uniform bound.

citations.quote:
Define the mutation covariance operators recursively. At time zero,
$$\widetilde V_0(\phi)=\operatorname{Cov}_{\widetilde\pi_0}(\phi).$$
For $t\ge1$,
$$\widetilde V_t(\phi)=\widehat V_{t-1}(k_t\phi)+\int\operatorname{Cov}_{k_t}(\phi)(x)\,\pi_{t-1}(dx).$$
The weighted-estimator covariance is
$$V_t(\phi)=\widetilde V_t\!\left(\upsilon_t(\phi-\pi_t(\phi))\right).$$
For a measurable vector function $h$ on $\Theta_t$, define the forward operator from $\Theta_{t-1}$ by
$$E_t h(x)=k_t(\upsilon_t h)(x)=\int\upsilon_t(z)h(z)\,k_t(x,dz).$$
For $k<t$, write $E_{k+1:t}=E_{k+1}\circ\cdots\circ E_t$; set $E_{t+1:t}$ to the identity operator.
For multinomial offspring resampling set
$$\widehat V_t^{\mathrm{multi}}(\phi)=V_t(\phi)+\operatorname{Cov}_{\pi_t}(\phi).$$
For residual offspring resampling, let $r(u)=u-\lfloor u\rfloor$. When $c_t=\widetilde\pi_t(r(\upsilon_t))>0$, define the formal source candidate
$$R_t^{\mathrm{cand}}(\phi)=\widetilde\pi_t\!\left(r(\upsilon_t)\phi\phi^\top\right)-\frac{\widetilde\pi_t(r(\upsilon_t)\phi)\,\widetilde\pi_t(r(\upsilon_t)\phi)^\top}{c_t}.$$
Set $R_t=R_t^{\mathrm{cand}}$ and $\widehat V_t^{\mathrm{res}}=V_t+R_t$ only when $\widetilde\pi_t(\upsilon_t\in\{1,2,\ldots\})=0$; then $c_t>0$ and the finite-sample floor discontinuities are avoided. If $\upsilon_t=1$ $\widetilde\pi_t$-almost everywhere, all normalized weights are exactly equal and residual offspring are deterministic; in that special case put $R_t=0$. No residual covariance is assigned when $c_t=0$ but $\upsilon_t$ is not almost everywhere one: the finite-sample normalization can move positive integer weights across floor boundaries. The B-page counterexamples show why the general positive-integer-atom branch remains unassigned.

Use the operators and multinomial variance recursion of [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]] at every selection time. For $\phi\in\Psi_t^{(d)}$, put $\bar\phi=\phi-\pi_t(\phi)$. Then
$$V_t(\phi)=\sum_{k=0}^{t}\widetilde\pi_k\!\left[\upsilon_k^2\,E_{k+1:t}(\bar\phi)E_{k+1:t}(\bar\phi)^\top\right],$$
where the $k=t$ term uses $E_{t+1:t}\bar\phi=\bar\phi$. Each summand is a finite positive-semidefinite matrix under the stated class conditions.

Fix a finite horizon $t$ and use the target/proposal flow and classes $\Phi_s^{(d)},\Psi_s^{(d)}$ of [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]], with $1\in\Phi_s^{(1)}$ for every $0\le s\le t$. Run the SIR procedure with multinomial resampling at each time. For $\phi\in\Psi_t^{(d)}$, let $\omega_t^N$ be the corrected weighted empirical law and $\check\eta_t^N$ the post-resampling empirical law. Then
$$\sqrt N\{\omega_t^N(\phi)-\pi_t(\phi)\}\Rightarrow\mathcal N_d(0,V_t(\phi)),\qquad
\sqrt N\{\check\eta_t^N(\phi)-\pi_t(\phi)\}\Rightarrow\mathcal N_d(0,\widehat V_t^{\rm multi}(\phi)),$$
where $\widehat V_t^{\rm multi}(\phi)=V_t(\phi)+\operatorname{Cov}_{\pi_t}(\phi)$. The horizon is fixed as $N\to\infty$; the theorem asserts no time-uniform finite-particle accuracy.

derivations.claim: The identity kernel leaves the uniform law invariant and has incremental weight one. Thus [F1] gives $E_{k+1:t}(\phi-\pi_t\phi)=\phi-1/2$ for every $k\le t$. Since $(\phi-1/2)^2=1/4$ everywhere, each of the $t+1$ summands in [F2] equals $1/4$. Therefore $V_t(\phi)=(t+1)/4$.

By [F3], at every fixed $t$ the weighted estimate has a valid CLT with variance $(t+1)/4$, and the post-resampling estimate has variance $(t+2)/4$. Both variance sequences are unbounded as $t$ ranges over the integers. The fixed-horizon theorem therefore supplies no uniform-in-time variance bound or finite-particle accuracy guarantee.
